acceptance.admission: Pre-admit both complete iteration requests and validate the new output location before source authentication or either solve.
acceptance.artifacts: Preserve each complete adapter report, raw rows, normalized policy and any partial observation in a lossless bounded case/reference.json.gz artifact; retain one bounded raw fallback if gzip output fails.
acceptance.failure: Keep first error, then record source/index/cleanup errors as secondary; preserve available reports in the returned API with an explicit not-durable marker when both artifact paths fail.
acceptance.models_and_training: Exactly one fresh model and at most one shared CFR+ training call per case; two cases total. No retries; stop after the first execution error.
acceptance.normalization: Record the explicit per-player 304-row normalization batches and their bounded row-family counts.
acceptance.quality: Retain exact NashConv and an explicit <=1/200 target result for each completed case; a miss is recorded without rerunning.
acceptance.runtime: Record CPython/OS metadata and wall/CPU elapsed receipts; elapsed values are not performance claims.
acceptance.source: Clean identical committed HEAD/status and 58 named LF hashes before/after; preserve the original failed v1 source and evidence.

failed_v1_prerequisite.qualification: One stopped T140 attempt; no T560, completed numeric verification or quality-gate result. Never relabel or retry the frozen v1 batch.

model_admission.interpretation: Named model/world/policy/path bounds only, not full-call work, memory or RSS.

replay_boundary.meaning: Bounded result-schema checks, separate from the unchanged named logical training forecast; not all arithmetic or a performance/memory bound.
replay_boundary.retention: Retain the full raw replay result before validation; expose only its eight metrics to the preserved v1 adapter and restore the wrapper on every exit.

scope.bounds: Named logical work, proof/diagnostic families, preparation ranks, source and output bytes only; not all arithmetic, allocation, wall time or RSS.
scope.claims: One finite fixed-board, fixed-stack, fixed-action-size game. No unrestricted Hold'em, convergence, speed, or memory claim follows.
scope.provenance: Project-owned implementation and standard library; shared CFR+ recurrence remains authenticated by the separate versioned budget.
